items.title: Trump administration to rescind rule protecting old growth forests
items.summary_raw:
Almost 45m acres of national forests could be potentially opened to road construction, drilling and logging

The Trump administration said on Tuesday it plans to rescind the “roadless rule” that has protected old growth forests in the US for 25 years, potentially opening up almost 45m acres of national forests to road construction, drilling and logging.

Conservationists had feared the announcement was coming since last summer after Brooke Rollins, Trump’s secretary of agriculture, targeted a rule brought in by Bill Clinton’s administration, describing it as “overly restrictive” and an “absurd obstacle” to development.

items.summary_raw:
UAE says Iran fired two ballistic missiles at territory

The UAE's defence ministry said on Tuesday that Iran targeted its terrority with two ballistic missiles, after reports that the country issued a missile threat alert earlier.

In a post to X, the ministry said that air defences “detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran toward the country, with the first falling outside the country’s territorial waters, while the second fell within the territorial waters”.

The statement added that the country is on high alert and ready to deal with any threats.

items.title: Syria publicly confirmed possessing nuclear material left over from the Assad regime.   IAEA chief Grossi said "tons of nuclear materials that could be put to bad use" were found a…
items.summary_raw: Syria publicly confirmed possessing nuclear material left over from the Assad regime.   IAEA chief Grossi said "tons of nuclear materials that could be put to bad use" were found at an undeclared site.  Syria voluntarily informed the IAEA in July and granted inspectors access.   Foreign Minister al-Shaibani said the material will remain in Syrian custody under IAEA safeguards, adding that Syria "affirms its sovereign and legal right to a peaceful nuclear program."  The material is linked to the Al-Kibar reactor that Israel destroyed in 2007, believed to have been built with North Korean assistance.   Grossi said Syria has regained its place as a fully compliant state:   We are now turning the page on the past.

Turkish media report that efforts to offload the Russian air-defense systems have produced no solution. Meanwhile, Donald Trump’s plan to potentially restore F-35 sales to Turkey remains stalled more than a month after he announced it. The central obstacle is U.S. law, which prevents Ankara from receiving the stealth fighters while it continues to possess the S-400. Options discussed have included transferring the systems to a third country or rendering them permanently inoperable, but no agreement has been reached.   The irony for Ankara is difficult to miss. Turkey sacrificed access to the world’s most advanced Western fighter program to acquire a Russian air-defense system that it can now neither meaningfully integrate into NATO nor easily sell. Kyrou, Professor of History and Director of the Program in East European and Russian Studies at Salem State University; Dr. Konstantinos Tsitselikis, Professor of Human Rights and International Organizations at the University of Macedonia; Dr. Elizabeth H. Prodromou Professor in the International Studies Program at Boston College; Prof. Dr. Johannes Niehoff-Panagiotidis of the Freie Universitat Berlin; Dr. Harry G. Dimopoulos, International Businessman and 1955 Pogrom Survivor; and Stelios Taketzis, Producer and former Executive Director of Cosmos FM.

items.title: US lawmaker calls for action against settler violence in the West Bank
items.summary_raw:
US lawmaker calls for action against settler violence in the West Bank

Amid escalating Israeli settler violence, US House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called on the Trump administration to pressure Israel into protecting Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

"The ongoing siege of Palestinian homes in the West Bank by violent, lawbreaking settlers is unacceptable. Enough," Jeffries said in a post on X.

"The Trump administration must compel the Israeli government to protect the lives, property and livelihood of innocent Palestinian civilians."

At least 18 people have been killed and 880 more wounded during settler attacks in 2026. The figures mark a sharp rise from the previous year. In 2025, Ocha documented around 830 Palestinians wounded by settlers across the entire year.

items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇺🇦⚡️ Ukraine is beginning to move critical energy infrastructure underground, with frontline Zaporizhzhia becoming the first city to build underground protection for key power facilities as Kyiv prepares its grid for further Russian attacks.   According to regional military administration chief Ivan Fedorov, underground protective structures are being constructed at two substations, while transformers at other critical facilities are being reinforced with massive concrete shelters. More than half of the region’s key transformers have already received protective structures, reducing their vulnerability to Russian missiles and drones.   This is Ukraine adapting its infrastructure to a long war. Instead of relying solely on scarce and expensive air-defense interceptors, Kyiv is increasingly making the targets themselves harder to destroy. If the Zaporizhzhia model proves effective and expands nationwide, Russia will have to spend considerably more weapons to achieve the same level of damage to Ukraine’s energy grid, precisely the kind of unfavorable exchange Kyiv needs ahead of future winter strike campaigns.  See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Successive intense heatwaves and an increasingly severe, continent-wide drought have left many of Europe’s farmers in an “unprecedented” crisis, with vegetable and grain growers in particular warning of “catastrophic” harvests.

French vegetable production is down by “a very significant extent” compared with previous years, French growers have said, with shortfalls put at 25% for courgettes, 35% for lettuces, 40% for peas, 60% for broccoli and 50% to 100% for artichokes.

The Pentagon announced a $22.9bn contract with Raytheon on Monday to accelerate deliveries of Tomahawk missiles, amid reports that US missile stocks have been strained by the war with Iran.

Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the deal would speed up deliveries “at unprecedented speed” to meet current operational demands.

A recent analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that US stocks of Patriot and THAAD interceptors have been cut by roughly half or more since the conflict with Iran began in late February.

items.title: Trump contradicts Vance on top US goal in Iran war
items.summary_raw:
Trump contradicts Vance on top US goal in Iran war

US President Donald Trump said preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon is Washington’s “number one Goal”, appearing to contradict Vice President JD Vance, who last week said keeping oil and gasoline prices low for Americans was the administration’s top priority.

“The number one Goal is, and always will be, that Iran cannot have, in any way, shape, or form, a Nuclear Weapon,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Vance told Fox News last week that the administration’s first goal was to “keep oil and gasoline cheap for Americans”, with ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon coming second.

items.title: Trump Orders Pentagon To Scale Back Joint Exercises With South Korea
items.summary_raw:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon on Sunday to scale back annual joint military exercises with South Korea, saying the ally declined to help with the war against Iran and citing his good relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un. Trump said in a social media post that the exercises, which began Monday, are not only costly but “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile” to North Korea, which he said “has been unthreatening and respectful” during his time in the White House.
“Therefore, and based on the fact that it is too late to cancel, I have instructed Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to substantially reduce the Joint Military Exercises!” Trump wrote. The president added that he recently asked South Korea’s president if they would join the U.S. in the “denuclearization” of Iran, “and they said, ‘No thanks!’”

The post Trump Orders Pentagon To Scale Back Joint Exercises With South Korea appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Iraqi Kurdistan leader says Iranian drones targeted his office
items.summary_raw:
Iraqi Kurdistan leader says Iranian drones targeted his office

The prime minister of Iraq's Kurdistan Regional Government, Masrour Barzani, said on Monday that Iranian drones targeted his office and the home of the head of the Kurdistan region’s Security and Intelligence Agency.

“Following an investigation by the Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Unit, my personal office and the home of the head of the Security and Intelligence Agency were targeted by Iranian drone attacks earlier today,” he said in a post on X, adding that the attacks were “reckless and unacceptable”.

He called the strikes a “dangerous escalation” and said they posed a direct threat to the security and stability of Iraq's Kurdish region.

The semiautonomous region has faced missile and drone attacks since the US-Israel war on Iran

items.title: Kushner to meet Netanyahu after talks with Hamas leaders
items.summary_raw:
Kushner to meet Netanyahu after talks with Hamas leaders

US envoy Jared Kushner is set to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after holding talks with Hamas leaders in Egypt, as Washington seeks to revive a Gaza peace plan endorsed by Hamas but rejected by Israel.

Netanyahu has insisted that any settlement must ensure Hamas is “genuinely disarmed”.

Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, met Hamas’s new leader Khalil al-Hayya in the Egyptian city of el-Alamein on Sunday, AFP reported.

The US envoy urged Hamas to take “concrete, verifiable steps” and conveyed that “Gaza can never again be a source of terror for Israel”, while the group reiterated its commitment to the proposed plan, the report said.

items.title: ‘Our new normal’: how marine heatwaves affect life in British seas
items.summary_raw:
As warming seas push native species to cooler waters farther north, once-rare visitors have become more common

‘It sounds silly but I thought it was a person in the water waving,” says Kurt Lander, skipper of the Yellowfin charter boat, based out of Brighton. But when he grabbed his binoculars, he realised the fluttering movement he had noticed in the middle of the Channel shipping lane was a pair of sunfish.

The huge fish were lying on their sides and flapping their fins. “Apparently, they do it as a visual attraction to birds,” he says. “They’re trying to get the birds to eat the parasites off them.”

items.title: Iran says 60-day deadline under US deal is no longer relevant
items.summary_raw:
Iran says 60-day deadline under US deal is no longer relevant

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said a 60-day period linked to the 17 June memorandum between Tehran and Washington was no longer relevant, accusing the United States of violating the agreement weeks after it was signed. 

“There is no provision in the memorandum of understanding referring to a ‘60-day deadline’, and the Islamic Republic of Iran never formulates its policies under pressure, ultimatums or time limits,” he said.

Baghaei said the memorandum envisaged a 60-day period for talks on “the lifting of sanctions” and “the nuclear issue”, which could have been extended if no agreement was reached.

However, he said “gross and widespread” US violations meant talks never began.

items.title: Greek Foreign Ministry: Turkish “Marine Parks” Illegal, Create No New Facts in Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Greece has sent a clear message to Ankara that the designation of Turkish “national marine parks” in areas beyond Turkish territorial waters has no legal effect and cannot create faits accomplis, following the publication of the relevant Presidential Decrees in the Turkish Official Gazette. Under the Presidential Decrees of 15 August, Turkiye designated two “national marine parks” in the northeastern Aegean and the Eastern Mediterranean, whose boundaries extend beyond Turkish territorial waters. In a statement, the Greek Foreign Ministry described the establishment of the parks as unlawful insofar as they cover international waters, stressing that, under the Law of the Sea, no state has the right to unilaterally establish marine protected areas outside its national jurisdiction. At the same time, Athens underlined that the Turkish marine parks are also unlawful insofar as they extend into the Greek continental shelf. Consequently, the Foreign Ministry stressed, the Turkish action “produces absolutely no legal effect”, either with regard to international waters or Greek sovereign rights over the continental shelf.

Wildlife groups in Florida are celebrating record numbers of sea turtle nests this season, but experts warn Donald Trump’s recent gutting of the Endangered Species Act (ESA) could reverse decades of their recovery from the edge of extinction.

With more than two months of the summer nesting season still to run, loggerhead turtles have already made 13,770 nests, hundreds more than recorded in any previous year, along an 8.5-mile stretch of shoreline monitored by the Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach, on Florida’s Atlantic coast.

items.title: Sky News found that more than 1,300 Strava users shared workout data from US military bases across the Middle East, revealing routes, routines, troop movements and even activity at…
items.summary_raw: Sky News found that more than 1,300 Strava users shared workout data from US military bases across the Middle East, revealing routes, routines, troop movements and even activity at bases not shown on public maps. Many users posted under their real names, potentially making individual personnel identifiable.  Security experts say Iran could have used this information alongside other intelligence to monitor US forces and identify targets.   Sky News highlighted cases in Bahrain and Jordan where changes in Strava activity appeared to reveal where personnel had relocated before locations were later attacked by Iran.  The issue is not new: the Pentagon warned in 2018 that fitness-app location data could endanger troops.   Despite restrictions, personnel from the US and UK have continued sharing activities from sensitive sites, including RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. Sky News also found Strava activity inside Israel’s Dimona nuclear research centre.  Source: Sky News

According to The Washington Post, one option under review would fundamentally alter the appearance and flight-deck configuration of America’s newest carrier class.  Naval planners are examining whether the carrier’s command tower, known as the “island,” could be moved forward from its current aft position toward the center of the ship. The existing placement was deliberately chosen to improve flight-deck efficiency and safety, creating more space around the catapults, accelerating aircraft launches and reducing turbulence during landings. The Trump administration has also ordered the Navy to develop options for replacing the Ford class’s modern electromagnetic aircraft launch system with traditional steam catapults, emphasizing what it describes as proven, reliable and affordable technology. items.title: Opinion: How Iran and Ukraine are strategically sinking their rivals at sea
items.summary_raw:
Opinion: How Iran and Ukraine are strategically sinking their rivals at sea

The Iran war may be fought primarily remotely via the air, but its strategic outcome is increasingly being decided at sea. 

The latest strikes and counterstrikes have clarified rather than altered that central fact. Washington may escalate through a ground intervention, wider attacks on Iran’s critical infrastructure, or a strike against the deeply buried nuclear-linked complex at Pickaxe Mountain in Isfahan province.

Each option could inflict further damage and expand the war. None, however, is likely to eliminate Iran’s distributed maritime architecture or make the Strait of Hormuz strategically irrelevant.

Australia’s first case of the deadly H5 bird flu in a little penguin has been confirmed on Victoria’s Phillip Island, only days after the state government announced it would begin vaccinating the species.

Confirmation of the virus in the little penguin will spark a race to vaccinate thousands of birds, with the government announcing on Saturday it would begin the rollout on Monday.

items.title: Libya's Haftar played role in securing US hostage's release, report says
items.summary_raw:
Libya's Haftar played role in securing US hostage's release, report says

Authorities in eastern Libya under military commander Khalifa Haftar helped secure the release of an American missionary held hostage held by an Islamic State affiliate in West Africa's Sahel region, escorting him to freedom through Libya, Reuters reported, citing five sources.

Four of the sources said that a deal was brokered, with one saying saying a ransom was paid. 

However, a senior source in Haftar's forces said they had carried out a military operation in Mali to free the hostage, Kevin Rideout. 

Reuters said the State Department declined to comment while the White House did not respond to a request for comment about Haftar's involvement.

Two Italian Eurofighters scrambled from Lithuania along with two Turkish F-16s from Estonia. One of the Italian jets identified and engaged the drone. Before Friday's incident, Ukrainian forces had launched attacks against Russian ports near St. Petersburg. Russian authorities claimed to have intercepted 15 Ukrainian drones during those attacks. items.title: Strong Firefighting Forces on Alert in Halkidiki but Wildfire Situation Has Improved
items.summary_raw:
HALKIDIKI – The wildfire situation in Siviri, Halkidiki, has improved. According to an update from the Fire Service, there is currently no active fire front, although numerous scattered hotspots remain. A total of 227 firefighters, 57 vehicles, 13 foot teams, six firefighting aircraft and one helicopter are operating in the area. All forces operating in Siviri, Kassandra, where the fire broke out the afternoon of Thursday, August 13, remain on alert and at full readiness. The situation Friday morning was significantly improved, and continuous water drops are being carried out to extinguish the remaining small pockets of fire. All forces are maintaining heightened readiness ahead of the significant strengthening of winds expected from midday.

The post Strong Firefighting Forces on Alert in Halkidiki but Wildfire Situation Has Improved appeared first on The National Herald.

President Donald Trump dismissed concerns Friday over living conditions and the mental health of service members on a US aircraft carrier deployed against Iran and said the ship would soon rotate out.

Asked by reporters whether family members were worried about the situation on the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, Trump said: "No, they're not."

Trump also rejected that the ship - now in its ninth month at sea - had been deployed for too long. "No, no, no, not nearly enough," he said.

items.title: Andy Burnham looks to cut new EV sales targets
items.summary_raw:
Move to dilute ZEV mandate from 80% down to as little as 50% could add millions of tonnes of CO2 to emissions and comes amid record UK heatwaves

Andy Burnham’s government has said it will look at cutting electric vehicle sales targets, in proposals that could add millions of tonnes a year to the UK’s future carbon dioxide emissions.

The government launched a consultation on Friday on cutting the target for new EVs to as little as 50% of all new cars in 2030, down from 80% under existing rules. The consultation will include several options, including leaving the headline target unchanged, or cutting it to 70%, 60% or 50%.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender An Italian Eurofighter assigned to NATO’s Baltic Air Policing mission shot down a drone of unconfirmed, but likely Russian origin after it entered Latvian airspace Friday, according to NATO and Latvian authorities.  Two Italian Eurofighters scrambled from Lithuania along with two Turkish F-16s from Estonia. One of the Italian jets identified and engaged the drone.  Latvian forces are now searching for the wreckage near Rugāji, about 35 km from the Russian border, so the drone’s origin has not yet been established.  The incident comes amid a growing number of drone incursions into Baltic airspace. Latvia says Ukrainian drones have entered the region several times this year, while officials also point to Russian electronic warfare as a possible factor causing Ukrainian systems to stray across borders.  Before Friday's incident, Ukrainian forces had launched attacks against Russian ports near St. Petersburg. Russian authorities claimed to have intercepted 15 Ukrainian drones during those attacks.  This is the third reported NATO interception of a drone in the Baltics in recent months, following a Romanian F-16 shootdown in Estonia in May and a French Rafale shootdown in

US Vice President JD Vance said that keeping oil and gas prices low for Americans is now Washington's top priority in its war on Iran. 

"I know that oil is down today and it's way down from the highs in the early days of the conflict," has said on Fox News. "That's goal number one -- keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country."

He added that the next primacy focus for the US is to "ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon".

items.title: Watch: Turkey's Fidan warns of 'radical steps' if Israel does not comply with Gaza deal
items.summary_raw:
Watch: Turkey's Fidan warns of 'radical steps' if Israel does not comply with Gaza deal

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned on Thursday that Turkey, Qatar, and Egypt may be compelled to take "radical steps" if the United States does not pressure Israel to comply with the Gaza peace deal.

Fidan emphasised that while the Palestinian side has fulfilled its commitments, Israel has shown no progress in advancing to the second phase of the agreement.

“We naturally expect the United States to exert the necessary pressure on Israel.”

At least four people died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport, and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings.

The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. US Vice President JD Vance said that Washington is using "diplomatic, military and economic" means to pressure Iran.

"The Iranians sometimes make commitments that they don't honour," Vance told Fox News. "They make a deal, they don't honour the deal."

He also expressed that he was confident the confrontation would end with Washington "in a stronger position," with Tehran left without a nuclear weapon and the vital Strait of Hormuz reopened. 

"What I think is really happening is that you're seeing a president of the United States at the height of his authority with a lot of tools — diplomatic, military, and economic," he said, adding that these means are being used "very selectively, very strategically".

items.title: Fossils show huge carbon emissions harm forests, not ‘green the planet’
items.summary_raw:
Study of 56m-year-old leaves counters claims from Trump administration members of ‘benefits’ of fossil fuel pollution

Adding huge quantities of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere is set to cause the Earth’s forests to wither and die rather than flourish, according to a new study that counters erroneous claims that fossil fuel pollution will green the planet.

An analysis of fossilized leaf cells from a period known as the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (or PETM), which occurred about 56m years ago, has helped reconstruct how the world’s forests responded when planet-heating gases were previously being released at a rapid rate.

Before these reforms, BND agents sometimes possessed accurate information about threats, but they were not legally authorized to intervene. Met Office forecaster Alex Burkill said:

“Temperatures [in areas covered by the amber warning] could reach highs of around 36, 37, possibly 38C.

Now when you get these sorts of high temperatures, well that’s when we could see impacts to our infrastructure, our railway lines, our roads, they are not designed for this sort of heat.

Millions of households in England and Wales face higher bills after water companies were given the green light to spend £3.4bn more than planned, including to support new homes and datacentres.

The new spending will come on top of the £104bn programme of investment approved by the regulator that had already meant water bills will rise by 36% over the second half of the decade.

items.title: Britain's scorched fields mean a food crisis – and the government is ignoring the one measure that would help | George Monbiot
items.summary_raw:
This summer’s extreme weather and wars in Iran and Ukraine have made our need for food stockpiles more pressing than ever

When a business makes long-term plans, they call it prudence. When a government makes long-term plans, they call it communism. Any sustained state intervention attracts the prefix “Soviet-style”, and triggers vicious attacks across the billionaire media. So governments have developed a bias against long-term thinking. This may explain why we no longer maintain strategic food reserves.

In Britain, where soils have parched, market analysts warn that we’re facing the most severe food security crisis in decades. items.title: India fuels worldwide jump in planned coal production
items.summary_raw:
Rise in new mine proposals, mainly in states of Odisha and Jharkhand, comes despite plateau in global demand

Enough new coalmining projects were proposed last year to increase global supplies by 2.5bn tonnes a year, an increase of 11% from the year before, even as demand for coal plateaus, according to a new report.

Global Energy Monitor, an NGO, found that India ignited a rise in new coalmine proposals in 2025 despite a global slowdown in the number of mine openings because of falling demand for the fossil fuel.

items.title: Israel seeking to 'remove Palestine from world's agenda', Erdogan says
items.summary_raw:
Israel seeking to 'remove Palestine from world's agenda', Erdogan says

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Wednesday accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's government of seeking to "remove Palestine" from the world's agenda. 

"The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region," Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart Mahmoud Abbas in Ankara. 

"No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people's hearts as they try to destroy it," he said, vowing Turkey would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

items.title: Erdogan eyes expansion of regional defence pact
items.summary_raw:
Erdogan eyes expansion of regional defence pact

President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has said he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday.

"Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries," the Turkish leader told Asharq Al-Awsat. "Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella." 

Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkey expected Egypt to join the pact "in the next stage", telling the Anadolu state news agency only "a few technical issues" stood in the way. 

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thu

items.title: Heat, algae and AI: proposed datacenter could damage Everglades, experts warn
items.summary_raw:
Plans for hyperscale datacenter in Palm Beach county prompt concerns over water and electricity demands

About 16 miles (26km) south-west of Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Largo estate, near the northern edge of the Florida Everglades, developers have proposed a hyperscale datacenter on a 202-acre (82-hectare) parcel of land surrounded by water. Local environmentalists warn that the proposed 600MW datacenter in western Palm Beach county could damage the wetlands, which the federal government and the state of Florida have spent a combined $6bn to restore after decades of drainage and development.

One concern is that the datacenter could exacerbate an existing issue of toxic bacterial blooms in a water system which has already been stressed by drought, fertilizer runoff and warm water temperatures. In recent summers, the bright blooms of blue-green algae have covered nearly half of Lake Okeechobee, which feeds into the Everglades.

My child and I were bonding over our hit-and-miss approach to reaping crops. But with heatwaves pushing more of Britain into drought, it’s starting to feel like a luxury we can’t afford

For the first time in my life, I live in a home that has real outdoor space. What a concept! There are no downsides to a garden. Back in spring, I made grand plans – I watched all the TikToks, I bought seeds and trays and pots and grow bags, I ordered soil, a trowel and a watering can. I knew what I was after: super-tiny-scale subsistence farming with a side of Zen. A little fruit, a little veg, lots of flowers to attract pollinators. And I knew I wanted my elder child to gain an understanding of how things come to be and how to cope if and when they fail.

We love a tomato side salad, so that was the first thing we attempted. The seedlings flourished and then died in the first heatwave of the season. An omen, surely. The dahlias, ranunculus and freesias refused to grow, let alone bloom. My enthusiasm began to wane.

The company added that repeated targeting have lead to severe damage to the Zawiya power station, and has forced it to withdraw its technical teams.

It warned that the attacks may cause more delays in maintenance and restoration of electricity services.

The UAVs, identified as Russian-made Gerbera drones and possibly carrying explosives, were spotted around 08:00 in Romania’s exclusive economic zone, about 90 nautical miles from Constanța.  EOD divers destroyed the two drones in controlled detonations, while a separate drone wing was recovered after being deemed safe.  The Romanian Naval Component Command contacted Ukraine, which confirmed that the aircraft did not belong to Ukrainian forces.

They said they are being forced "to curtail a wide range of human rights and legal work in violation of... First and Fifth Amendment rights under the US Constitution and under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act", given that anyone who appears to associate with ICC cases or officials could now face legal repercussions.
